messages:
carol: Quick follow-up from the hosting/dedicated/private adapter sync — small design question: how should telemetry surface differentiate origin vs fallback routes without leaking tenant metadata? I sketched a minimal contract: coarse origin enum + routing_version + low-cardinality reason tag. Thoughts?

sam: +1 on the coarse enum. we need both origin and served_by_variant (e.g., gptq-8, fp16). also capture fallback_reason (capacity, model_mismatch, auth) so SLO dashboards can attribute.

tania: Agree, but cardinality is the killer. If served_by_variant can blow up, limit it to a bucketed set (preferred, fallback, degraded). For latency histograms prefer tags: hosting=HOSTED|DEDICATED|PRIVATE, path=preferred|fallback, variant_bucket=perf|balanced|accurate.

ryan: Ops perspective — make metrics queryable without tenant IDs. Emit normalized metric names and keep tags strictly low-cardinality. Example metric: redwood.request.latency_ms{hosting="DEDICATED",path="fallback",variant_bucket="perf"}. Do not emit raw tenant_id in metrics; put any tenant-specific logs into a separate audit sink.

mike (security): Strong NO to raw tenant identifiers in telemetry. For private deployments we may need tenant metadata in audit logs for compliance, but that data must be stored in the customer-controlled audit store and never sent to hosted metrics. Also: any sampling that includes traces with payload must be opt-in and permissioned.

carol: OK — sounds like consensus: 1) telemetry contract: origin enum (HOSTED|DEDICATED|PRIVATE), path enum (PREFERRED|FALLBACK|DEGRADED), variant_bucket (perf|balanced|accurate), routing_version, fallback_reason (capacity|model_mismatch|auth|none). 2) No raw tenant ids in hosted metrics; hashed/opt-in only for debug traces. 3) Audit logs for Private can include tenant context but must be separately controlled.

sam: Implementation note: runtime will need to annotate requests early. propose header approach so adapters can preserve the fields across handoffs. Example headers:
```http
X-Hosting-Origin: DEDICATED
X-Routing-Path: FALLBACK
X-Variant-Bucket: perf
X-Routing-Version: v2
X-Fallback-Reason: capacity
X-Telemetry-Sample: 1/100
```
This keeps the runtime free of high-cardinality strings in metrics while still letting traces include richer info when sampled.

carol: +1. Also propose we cap variant_bucket values to exactly these three strings and add a server-side mapping table for any new variant names. that prevents metric explosion if new model names enter the catalog.

tania: For traces, prefer storing the full model name only in sampled trace payloads and replace with model_hash in metrics/tags. add a TTL on stored trace payloads by default (30 days).

ryan: Ops tasks: 1) update pager playbooks so alerts reference hosting+path tags, not tenant. 2) retrofit existing dashboards to the normalized metric pattern. I'll take dashboard migration.

mike (security): I'll draft the telemetry policy snippet we can embed in the RFC: what is allowed in metrics vs what must go to customer audit sinks. also define opt-in flow for debug traces.

carol: Action items then: - carol: update RFC with concrete schema + header examples (this week) - ryan: dashboard migration plan (owner) - mike: telemetry policy text - sam/tania: small runtime patch to emit headers on handoff + mapping table.

ops-bot: Note: deploy window for runtime change is open next Tue 02:00-06:00 UTC. Tag @sam if you want the slot. :calendar:

carol: Thanks all — I'll push the RFC update and ping this thread when ready.
